raw_response:
I’m not going to spread too much this year. I only have 16.1 mu, and with 5 mouths at home I need steady harvest more than fancy ideas. I’ve only farmed 3 years, so I still follow what works nearby. The older farmers here say grain land should stay grain on part of the farm, so I’ll keep some wheat and then put summer maize right after it. That gives me food and safer income. For cash, I’ll keep eggplant as my main money crop because I already know it a bit and I can use the well when it turns dry. Cabbage and cauliflower I’ll do on smaller pieces. Those crops sell better in some years, but price can drop fast, so I don’t want too much area in one thing.

For fertilizer, I won’t calculate too fine. I mostly do what I saw last year and what neighbors do: base fertilizer first, then one or two topdressings if the crop looks weak. If I cut fertilizer too much and the crop turns yellow, that loss hurts more than spending a bit extra. But I also can’t throw money around, so for vegetables I’ll feed the better fields first, and for wheat and maize I’ll keep rates around the common local level, not too low, not too high. Water from the well helps, but pumping costs money, so I’ll save irrigation for key times: wheat at jointing and filling, maize if summer rain is short, and eggplant more regularly because it needs steady moisture. Labor is mostly family labor, and I’ll only hire a little help when wheat harvest and maize planting run into each other.
